With regard to earthenware vessels, … any … that does not have a receptacle has no distinction with regard to … its sides. … its inside,

With regard to earthenware vessels, any vessel that does not have a receptacle has no distinction with regard to the halakhic status of its sides. This is in contrast to the earthenware vessels mentioned in the Torah, where only the inside, and not the outside, is susceptible to ritual impurity. Rather, if its inside,
its outside became impure, … its inside … becomes impure.
its outside became impure, its inside also becomes impure.
